source.excerpt: More tears are shed over answered prayers
trail: Wikiquote identifies Gloria Steinem’s McCall’s interview with Truman Capote (November 1967) as its earliest located Teresa attribution; that magazine page was not inspected here.

The inspected American Dialect Society exchange quotes the Capote/Teresa credit and Fred Shapiro asks for documentation. It also points to a related Wilde line, which is a parallel rather than proof of this sentence’s creator.
Capote’s publisher identifies Answered Prayers as his unfinished final novel; the catalog does not authenticate the epigraph’s Teresa attribution.

author.heading: About Unknown
author.bio: The creator of this exact English wording has not been established. Teresa of Ávila (1515–1582), the person named in the attribution, was a Spanish Carmelite reformer and spiritual writer whose major works include The Life, The Way of Perfection and The Interior Castle. A modern English quotation credit needs an identifiable textual link to those writings.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The saying became associated with the title of Truman Capote’s Answered Prayers. That novel concerns ambition and high society, making the irony of a granted wish especially apt. Its literary use is evidence of circulation, not evidence that the sixteenth-century Teresa supplied these English words.
